newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU strikes deal on 1997 fish catch quotas.
newsitem.headline: EU strikes deal on 1997 fish catch quotas.

text.p: European Union fisheries ministers agreed on Friday after traditional all-night talks an Irish compromise easing cuts in 1997 fish catch quotas to please fishermen but protecting stocks, an Irish official said.
The European Commission, acting on scientific advice, had proposed further reductions in order to safeguard both run-down fish stocks and the future of the EU fishing industry.
"There's agreement on TACs (total allowable catches) and quotas," the official said 16 hours after ministers began formal negotiations.

One of the main battles was over the allocation of quotas under new EU fisheries agreements with the Baltic States following Sweden and Finland's entry into the EU. Germany, Denmark and Finland had problems with the share-out.
Denmark was also unhappy with the introduction of a quota for by-catches of herring by huge vessels hunting sprats for industrial processing into fish meal and oil.
Italy and Greece fought off quotas on tuna fishing in the Mediterranean while measures to restrict sardine fishing off the coasts of Spain and Portugal were eased.
